Load data: These data are from this 538 story: https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/airplane-etiquette-recline-seat/

The file is in excel format. If we want to we can use a command from the xlsx package(loaded above) to input the data directly.

fly <- readWorkbook("fly.xlsx", sheet="fly", na.strings = "NA")

Packages for importing from excel directly can be finicky(due to microsoft updates etc). Thats ok. It is often easier to just click “save as” in the excel program and save your spreadsheet as a csv. When we do this we can use the read.csv command we’ve used in previous classes.

Another note: similar packages exist for important data from STATA, SPSS, SAS, etc.

#Code Book

respondent_id RespondentID gender Gender age Age height Height children_under_18 Do you have any children under 18? household_income Household income bracket education Education Level location Location (census region) frequency How often do you travel by plane? recline_frequency Do you ever recline your seat when you fly? recline_obligation Under normal circumstances, does a person who reclines their seat during a flight have any obligation to the person sitting behind them? recline_rude Is it rude to recline your seat on a plane? recline_eliminate Given the opportunity, would you eliminate the possibility of reclining seats on planes entirely? switch_seats_friends Is it rude to ask someone to switch seats with you in order to be closer to friends? switch_seats_family Is it rude to ask someone to switch seats with you in order to be closer to family wake_up_bathroom Is it rude to wake a passenger up if you are trying to go to the bathroom? wake_up_walk Is it rude to wake a passenger up if you are trying to walk around? baby In general, is it rude to bring a baby on a plane? unruly_child In general, is it rude to knowingly bring unruly children on a plane? two_arm_rests In a row of three seats, who should get to use the two arm rests? middle_arm_rest In a row of two seats, who should get to use the middle arm rest? shade Who should have control over the window shade? unsold_seat Is it rude to move to an unsold seat on a plane? talk_stranger Generally speaking, is it rude to say more than a few words to the stranger sitting next to you on a plane? get_up On a 6 hour flight from NYC to LA, how many times is it acceptable to get up if you’re not in an aisle seat? electronics Have you ever used personal electronics during take off or landing in violation of a flight attendant’s direction? smoked Have you ever smoked a cigarette in an airplane bathroom when it was against the rules?

Technically, these would be considered ordinal variables, but for our purposes we can treat them as numeric. Thus, we need R to convert them to numeric

fly$nrecline_rude <- as.numeric(as.factor(fly$recline_rude)) #as.numeric(as.factor) converts, but can be tricky. Be sure you check the order makes sense

#much safer to do it this way
fly$nrecline_rude <- recode(fly$recline_rude, "No"=1,"Somewhat"=2, "Very"=3)

table(fly$nrecline_rude)
## 
##   1   2   3 
## 502 281  71
table(fly$recline_rude)
## 
##       No Somewhat     Very 
##      502      281       71
prop.table(table(fly$recline_rude))
## 
##         No   Somewhat       Very 
## 0.58782201 0.32903981 0.08313817
prop.table(table(fly$nrecline_rude))
## 
##          1          2          3 
## 0.58782201 0.32903981 0.08313817
#always a good idea to confirm values match up. For example this wouldn't work if we tried to recode height the same way
table(fly$age)
## 
##  > 60 18-29 30-44 45-60 
##   258   220   254   275
fly$agen <- recode(fly$age, "18-29"=1,"30-44"=2, "45-60"=3, "> 60"=4 )
#In this case you can use nested ifelse commands or dplyr's recode. 
table(fly$age)
## 
##  > 60 18-29 30-44 45-60 
##   258   220   254   275
table(fly$agen)
## 
##   1   2   3   4 
## 220 254 275 258
hist(fly$nrecline_rude, main="Majority Think Reclining is not Rude", xlab="Perceived Rudeness")

fly$ngender <- recode(fly$gender, "Female"=0, "Male"=1)

table(fly$ngender)
## 
##   0   1 
## 528 479
table(fly$gender)
## 
## Female   Male 
##    528    479

Convert a second variable to numeric

fly$nrecline_frequency<- recode(fly$recline_frequency, "Never"=0, "Once in a while"=1, "About half the time"=2, "Usually"=3, "Always"=4)

table(fly$nrecline_frequency)
## 
##   0   1   2   3   4 
## 171 257 118 175 137
table(fly$recline_frequency)
## 
## About half the time              Always               Never     Once in a while 
##                 118                 137                 171                 257 
##             Usually 
##                 175

Using ifelse to recode variables

#sometimes we want to change labels or collapse categories - ie make frequency binary
fly$frequentfliers <- ifelse(fly$frequency=="A few times per month"| fly$frequency=="A few times per week"|fly$frequency=="Every day", 1, 0)
table(fly$frequentfliers) #recall | means or 
## 
##    0    1 
## 1004   36
table(fly$frequency)
## 
## A few times per month  A few times per week             Every day 
##                    29                     4                     3 
##                 Never  Once a month or less   Once a year or less 
##                   166                   205                   633

We’ve done some work to make this dataset workable.

We can then export this to a variety of format: (http://www.statmethods.net/input/exportingdata.html)

write.csv(fly, "flyedited.csv") #This will automatically save to your working directory

Do a t-test to see if this relationship is statisticalsignificant. ie is there a meaningful(statistically significant) difference between men and women’s attitudes toward the rudeness of reclining your airplane seat? ie are they from the same population or different?

t.test(fly$nrecline_rude~ fly$gender) # t= t-statistic, df= degrees of freedom, p-value= only significant (usually) if less than .05, and confidence interval
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  fly$nrecline_rude by fly$gender
## t = -0.18012, df = 827.35, p-value = 0.8571
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group Female and group Male is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.09558460  0.07951618
## sample estimates:
## mean in group Female   mean in group Male 
##             1.493213             1.501247

There are a number of options with the t-test: t.test(x, y = NULL, alternative = c(“two.sided”, “less”, “greater”), mu = 0, paired = FALSE, var.equal = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95)

As a bit of foreshadowing, we can run the same two variables in a bivariate regression and get the same p-value.

summary(lm(nrecline_rude~gender, data=fly))
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = nrecline_rude ~ gender, data = fly)
## 
## Residuals:
##     Min      1Q  Median      3Q     Max 
## -0.5012 -0.5012 -0.4932  0.5068  1.5068 
## 
## Coefficients:
##             Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept) 1.493213   0.030717   48.61   <2e-16 ***
## genderMale  0.008034   0.044537    0.18    0.857    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Residual standard error: 0.6458 on 841 degrees of freedom
##   (197 observations deleted due to missingness)
## Multiple R-squared:  3.869e-05,  Adjusted R-squared:  -0.00115 
## F-statistic: 0.03254 on 1 and 841 DF,  p-value: 0.8569

Try to show this visually

#use dplyr
rude <- fly %>% drop_na(gender)%>% group_by(gender) %>% summarise (me = mean(nrecline_rude, na.rm=T), se=sd(nrecline_rude, na.rm=T)/sqrt(length(nrecline_rude)))
rude #Recall, %>% is called piping. It is a way to add together code. So here I'm saying in the dataset fly, group by gender, and then calculate(summarise) by finding the mean and standard error and put all that in a new dataframe called rude
## # A tibble: 2 × 3
##   gender    me     se
##   <chr>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1 Female  1.49 0.0277
## 2 Male    1.50 0.0300
p <-ggplot(aes(x=gender, y=me), data=rude, colour="blue") + geom_bar(stat="identity", colour="grey")
 p  

 p+geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=me-(1.96*se), ymax=me+se), 
                  colour="red", width=.3) +
 labs(x = "Gender", y = "Attitude toward Reclining Seats") +
  ggtitle("Reclining Seats by Gender")

What about differences by education?

Create a new binary variable

table(fly$education) #Look at variable
## 
##                  Bachelor degree                  Graduate degree 
##                              325                              284 
##               High school degree     Less than high school degree 
##                               98                                8 
## Some college or Associate degree 
##                              286
fly$edu <- ifelse(fly$education=="High school degree"|fly$education=="Less than high school degree", 0, 1) #creates a dummy (0, 1)
##more advanced use of ifelse creates categorical variable

table(fly$edu) #alway check to make sure. 
## 
##   0   1 
## 106 895
t.test(fly$nrecline_rude~ fly$edu)
## 
##  Welch Two Sample t-test
## 
## data:  fly$nrecline_rude by fly$edu
## t = 1.9499, df = 77.817, p-value = 0.05479
## alternative hypothesis: true difference in means between group 0 and group 1 is not equal to 0
## 95 percent confidence interval:
##  -0.003368177  0.323313903
## sample estimates:
## mean in group 0 mean in group 1 
##        1.641791        1.481818

Significant at .10, but not .05

table(fly$getupn)

hist(fly$getupn)

fregm <- fly %>% group_by(frequentfliers)%>% summarise(mean=mean(getupn, na.rm=T))

fly %>% ggplot(aes(x=getupn, fill=as.factor(frequentfliers)))+ geom_density(alpha=.8)+theme_minimal()+scale_fill_manual(values = c("cyan3", "lawngreen"), name="Frequent Flyers")+geom_vline(xintercept=2.82, color="cyan3")+geom_vline(xintercept=2.68, color="lawngreen")
